name: Uncut skills
description: Uncut's own skills: production recipes the agent loads when they fit (launch promo, product demo, motion, motion film facts, sound, brand) and the brand kit maker. Type / in the composer to use one.
author: Uncut

skills.name: launch-promo
skills.title: Launch promo
skills.description: A 15 to 30 s launch film: hook, problem, reveal, proof, call to action.
skills.instructions:
A launch film of 15 to 30 s for a feed. It sells one promise, not a feature list.

Structure (one job per beat)
- 0 to 2 s: the hook. The product doing its most surprising thing, or the sharpest claim, already moving on frame 0. No logo intro, no company description, no fade from black.
- 2 to 6 s: the problem, one line of type over something real (the slow old way, the error, the mess).
- 6 to 18 s: the reveal. Three beats at most on the real product, each showing one thing and naming it in 5 words or fewer.
- 18 to 23 s: proof. One real number, quote or result that the brief gives. Never invent one.
- Last 3 to 4 s: the call to action. Logo file, one line, the URL, held still: the longest hold in the film.
- Pick one arc and keep it: problem, agitation, product, proof, CTA; or before, after, bridge; or a demo loop.

Rules
- Name the brand on screen within the first 5 s.
- Shots of 0.8 to 2 s, cut on the music's beats (beat_grid); the reveal and the end card on downbeats.
- One line of type at a time, 6 words at most, held for at least 0.3 s a word and never under 1 s.
- Real footage only: captures, screenshots, the kit's logo files. A missing asset is asked for, not mocked up.

Do
- Crop into the part of the UI that matters; punch in rather than show a whole screen.
- Let the reveal breathe: a 1 to 1.5 s hold after the product lands.

Don't
- Don't open on a logo sting, a black frame or a slow zoom.
- Don't list features; show one promise three ways.
- Don't put a new line of text in the last 2 s.

Example
- 0.0 "Your CI takes 40 minutes" over the real red pipeline, 2.0 cut on a downbeat to the product run finishing, 4.5 "Now it takes 4", 7.0 three UI beats, 19.0 one customer number from the brief, 23.0 logo, "Try it free", URL.

Review checklist
- Frame 0 shows motion or the claim, with the sound off.
- The brand is on screen within the first 5 s.
- Every beat says one thing; no beat repeats another's look.
- Every product shot is real footage or a real screenshot, nothing mocked up.
- The proof is from the brief, not invented.
- The end card holds still for at least 2 s with a readable URL.

skills.name: product-demo
skills.title: Product demo
skills.description: A demo built on real UI recordings: tight crops, cursor and state changes that read.
skills.instructions:
A product demo built on real UI recordings (captures, screen recordings, device frames).

Structure
- Hook: the end result first (the finished thing, the number going green), 2 s.
- The task in one line: what the viewer will see done.
- Three to six steps, each a real recording: start state, the action, the new state. A UI flow usually spans several beats on the same screen.
- The result again, then the call to action.

Rules
- Crop or punch in to the region that changes; text in the UI must be readable at phone size (360 px wide). If it isn't, zoom to 150 to 250 % on that region.
- One state change per beat. Hold the new state 1 to 1.5 s after it lands, so the eye catches up.
- Speed up waiting only, and say so in words ("2x"); never mix speeds without saying it.
- Cursor: one cursor, moving in arcs with an ease, slowing into the target; a click shows a small press (scale 0.95, back on a snap spring). Hide stray or doubled cursors.
- Device frames hold the real capture; an empty phone or browser frame is a defect, never a style.

Do
- Cut on the action: cut as the click lands or as the panel starts to move, never in the dead time after.
- Label a step with a short callout next to the thing it names, kit body font, at least 40 px at 1080 wide.

Don't
- Don't show a whole desktop at 1:1; nobody can read it on a phone.
- Don't add a click sound to a text appearing or to typing; clicks go on real clicks.
- Don't put glow, blur or gradients on UI: it stops looking like the product.

Example
- Capture of "Deploy" pressed, punch in 180 % on the log, 3x on the build with "3x" in the corner, hold 1.2 s on "Live", end card.

Review checklist
- Every screen shown is a real capture of the product, no empty device frame.
- UI text that matters is readable at 360 px wide.
- Each step shows a visible state change and holds it at least 1 s.
- One cursor at most, and it moves to what the step is about.
- Any speed change is labelled on screen.

skills.name: talking-head
skills.title: Talking-head short
skills.description: A 9:16 short cut from a talking head, with burned-in captions and real b-roll.
skills.instructions:
A 9:16 short of 30 to 60 s cut from a talking head, with burned-in captions and real b-roll.

Structure
- The hook is the strongest line said, moved to the start if it stands alone, playing in the first 2 s.
- One idea per beat, 3 to 8 s each, whole sentences only.
- The last line is the call to action, then an end card with the logo file and URL for 2 s.

Cut
- Cut by the transcript (transcript_edit): fillers, false starts, repeats, pauses over 0.3 s, unless a pause lands a point.
- Hide jump cuts with a punch-in of 110 to 130 % on emphasis; alternate wide and tight, never two punch-ins in a row on the same framing.
- Use J and L cuts on b-roll: the voice runs on under the picture change, so the story never stops for a cut.

Captions
- From the transcript (captions_make), names and product words corrected by hand.
- Groups of 2 to 6 words or at most 2.5 s, breaking at a pause, a comma or a sentence end; each on screen at least 0.5 s.
- At most 2 lines (3 in 9:16), up to 90 % of the width, in the lower middle: clear of the top 15 % and the bottom 35 %, and of the right 18 % where the app's buttons are.
- Kit body font, bold, kit text colour with a box or soft shadow; one key word per line in the accent colour at most.

Do
- Eyes on the upper third line; keep the face in the same place across cuts.
- B-roll illustrates the exact thing being said, 1.5 to 4 s, with the speaker's audio under it.

Don't
- Don't caption with a template animation on every word; a cut-in is enough.
- Don't add whooshes on plain cuts; a soft hit on a punch-in at most.
- Don't let music compete: ducked well under the voice or none.

Example
- "We deleted our staging server." 0 to 2 s, punch-in 120 % on "deleted", b-roll of the real dashboard while the voice continues, CTA line, end card.

Review checklist
- The first 2 s carry the strongest line, with captions on frame 0.
- Captions are readable at 360 px wide and stay out of the platform's UI zones.
- No caption group longer than 6 words or shorter than 0.5 s on screen.
- No visible jump cut without a punch-in or b-roll over it.
- The voice is clear: music ducked under it, no effect over a word.

skills.name: social-cutdown
skills.title: Social cut-down
skills.description: One edit delivered as 9:16, 4:5, 1:1 and 16:9 cuts, each safe for its platform.
skills.instructions:
One edit delivered in several formats: 9:16, 4:5, 1:1 and 16:9, each built for its feed, not letterboxed.

Structure
- Build the master in the most demanding format the brief needs (usually 9:16 or 4:5), then make each other format its own project or cut.
- Per format: reframe each shot (punch in, move the crop), re-flow the type, re-check every hold.
- Shorter cuts (6 s, 15 s) keep the hook, the one strongest beat and the end card; drop beats, never speed them up.

Rules
- Safe areas at 1080 x 1920: text out of the top 15 % and the bottom 35 %, and clear of the right 18 % (TikTok and Shorts buttons). 4:5 and 1:1: 8 % from every edge.
- Captions or supers on every line that matters: many people watch muted.
- Type sizes from the shorter side: headline at least 84 px, body at least 44 px at 1080.
- Frame 0 is the thumbnail and the autoplay: the claim or motion, never black.

Do
- 4:5 (1080 x 1350) for X, LinkedIn and Instagram feeds; 9:16 for Reels, TikTok and Shorts; 16:9 for YouTube, sites and decks.
- Check every format at phone size before handing it over.

Don't
- Don't pillarbox a 16:9 edit into 9:16 with blurred bars.
- Don't keep a layout that crops the logo or the URL in a narrower format.
- Don't copy the master's text positions blindly; re-place them per format.

Example
- Master 4:5 25 s; 9:16 with captions raised above the bottom 35 %; 1:1 with the end card re-flowed; 6 s cut: hook, reveal, end card.

Review checklist
- Each format fills its frame; no letterbox or blurred bars.
- All text and logos sit inside that format's safe area.
- Text is readable at 360 px wide in every format.
- Shorter cuts keep the hook and the end card.

skills.name: explainer
skills.title: Explainer
skills.description: How it works in 30 to 90 s: one idea per beat, diagrams built step by step.
skills.instructions:
How it works, in 30 to 90 s: a concept, an architecture, a workflow. Clarity over flash.

Structure
- Hook: the question the viewer has, or the surprising answer, in the first 3 s.
- Context in one beat: what exists today and why it falls short.
- The idea in steps, one per beat: each beat adds one element to a diagram or one step to a flow.
- A real example on the product (a capture) that proves the idea.
- Recap in one line, then the call to action.

Rules
- Build diagrams step by step: each new box or arrow arrives when the voice or the caption names it, in the later half of its beat, not all at once at the start.
- One focal element per frame; everything that isn't the focus is still and dimmed.
- Voice or supers of 6 to 20 words a beat. Hold text at least 0.3 s a word.
- Arrows and paths draw along their direction with an ease; boxes land with a settle spring.
- Keep the same layout for the diagram across beats so the viewer's map holds; move the camera, not the boxes.

Do
- Use the kit's colours by meaning: one accent for the thing that's new, the rest neutral.
- Label every element in the diagram with real names from the product.

Don't
- Don't fill the screen with the full diagram on the first frame.
- Don't add icons or numbers the brief doesn't give.
- Don't let a beat run past 8 s with nothing new on screen.

Example
- "Where does a request go?" 0 to 3 s; client box, then edge box, arrow drawing between them as the caption names it; capture of the real trace; "One hop instead of four", CTA.

Review checklist
- Every diagram builds step by step; nothing appears before it is named.
- Each frame has one clear focal element.
- Labels use real product names; no invented figures.
- No stretch over 8 s without a visible change.

skills.name: title-sequence
skills.title: Title sequence and kinetic type
skills.description: Type as the picture: a hierarchy, holds you can read, motion that follows the words.
skills.instructions:
Titles and kinetic typography: type is the picture. Openers, manifestos, word-led promos, end cards.

Structure
- A hierarchy: one headline size, one support size, one small label size; never more than three.
- Rhythm in two speeds: quick runs (about 0.4 s a word or short phrase) for energy, statement holds (1.5 s or more) for what must be read. Alternate them.
- The climax word or line gets the one special treatment (the accent colour, a bigger size or a different move), once.
- The last card is the longest hold.

Rules
- Hold every line at least 0.3 s a word after its entrance finishes, never under 1 s; one line on screen at a time unless it's a list being built.
- Each beat has one entrance; nothing from the previous beat lingers.
- Motion follows reading order: words enter left to right or top to bottom, a few frames apart (2 to 4 frames stagger), and settle on a snap or land spring with no visible bounce.
- Cut type on the music's beats; the climax on a downbeat.
- Type at least 84 px for headlines and 44 px for support at 1080 wide; tracking tighter as size grows; kit fonts only.

Do
- Use scale, position and weight changes on the words themselves; let the empty space work.
- Exit faster than you entered, or cut out on the beat.

Don't
- Don't centre a gradient title on a dark field with a glow: the default AI look.
- Don't fade every line in and out; most lines simply cut in.
- Don't animate every letter, or use typewriter reveals for anything but code.
- Don't put dots, bullets or stars between words; use commas or line breaks.

Example
- "Builds." "Tests." "Deploys." at 0.4 s each on beats, then "All in one place" held 1.8 s, accent on "one", end card held 3 s.

Review checklist
- No more than three type sizes, kit fonts only.
- Every line is fully readable for at least 0.3 s a word.
- Only one moment gets special treatment.
- No centred gradient-plus-glow title, no fade on every line.
- Type sits inside the safe margin and reads at 360 px wide.

skills.name: motion-craft
skills.title: Motion craft
skills.description: Springs per object class, holds, readability, and the clichés to avoid.
skills.instructions:
Motion craft: every move has a reason, starts and lands well, and leaves time to read.

Springs by object class (Uncut's presets)
- Type and small UI (buttons, chips, cursor presses): snap, quick and critically damped, no visible bounce.
- Panels, cards, screenshots, device frames: settle, a little slower, no overshoot you can see.
- Headlines and hero moments: land, a firm arrival with at most a hint of overshoot.
- bounce only when the brand is playful and the brief says so; bounciness is the fastest way to look cheap.
- Opacity and colour changes: no spring, a short ease (150 to 250 ms).

Timing
- Entrances 8 to 12 frames at 30 fps (250 to 400 ms); exits shorter (6 to 8 frames) or a cut.
- Big moves over a long distance at most about 600 ms; anything slower feels like a drag.
- Stagger related elements 2 to 4 frames apart in reading order, image first, its label trailing.
- Hold after every arrival: at least 0.3 s a word for text, 1 s for a UI state, before the next change.

Rules
- One focal element moves at a time; everything else holds still.
- Ease in and out, never linear (except a deliberate constant scroll). Curved paths over straight diagonals for travel.
- Cut on motion: a cut at the peak of a move, the next shot moving the same way at the same speed.
- render(t) graphics are pure functions of t: springs from uncut:lib, seeded random, no timers.

Banned clichés
- A centred gradient title on a dark field.
- Everything fading in, or every text with the same entrance.
- Glow, bloom or drop shadows on UI and screenshots.
- Corner labels and pill tags with no reason to be there.
- A floating blob or orb as the background; a stray decorative cursor.
- Slow push-ins and breathing loops to fill time.
- Everything on screen in the first quarter of a scene.

Review checklist
- Every move settles cleanly; no linear drifts, jitter or visible bounce on type and UI.
- Only one thing moves at a time in each beat.
- Every text and UI state holds long enough to read before the next change.
- None of the banned clichés is on screen.
- Moves follow reading order and the music's beats.

skills.name: sound-design
skills.title: Sound design
skills.description: Few, quiet, synced sound effects; music matched to the pace; ducking under voice.
skills.instructions:
Sound design: sound makes the picture land. Fewer, quieter, exactly in sync. When in doubt, leave it out.

Music
- Pick music for the pace: punchy cuts every 1 to 2 s want 110 to 130 BPM with a clear pulse (beat_grid tells a track's tempo); calm demos or explainers 80 to 100 BPM. Never a slow lo-fi loop under a fast edit.
- Run beat_grid once the music is placed; cuts and state changes on beats, the reveal and end card on downbeats.
- Fade in about 1 s unless it starts on a hit; end on a downbeat or a 2 s fade; never make the video longer for the music.
- Under a voice: duck it (audio.duck, about -12 dB) or keep it 15 to 20 dB under the voice; the voice always wins.

Sound effects: when
- Only on a real visual event: a cut it carries, an element landing, a real click by a cursor or finger, the reveal, the logo.
- At most one effect per event and at most 4 in any 10 s; a 20 s promo usually needs 3 to 6 in total. A motion film (ui profile) instead gets one soft effect per real press, drag or morph.
- One big hit (boom, impact) in a film, on the moment that matters most; a riser only into that moment.
- Vary by meaning: whooshes for movement between scenes, a soft tick for a UI press, a hit for the reveal. The same file at most twice.
- No meme sounds (airhorn, bruh, laugh, record scratch) unless the user asked for that joke.
- No UI clicks on text appearing or as typing; typing gets a real keyboard sound or nothing.
- A cut on the beat needs no whoosh: the music already carries it.

Sound effects: how
- 6 to 12 dB under the music (gainDb), since the bundled effects are peak-normalised and jump out at the same gain.
- Start a whoosh or hit 1 to 2 frames before the frame it hits; a riser ends on the frame it builds to.
- Short fades on effects that ring past their moment; nothing over a spoken word.

Mix
- Aim for about -14 LUFS integrated and a true peak under -1 dBTP for social and YouTube.
- Read the mix blind: list every sound with its time (project_check's sound findings, the critic's sound sheet). If the list alone sounds like a meme reel or a click track, cut it down.

Review checklist
- Every sound effect lands on something that changes on screen.
- No more than 4 effects in any 10 s, no file more than twice, one big hit at most (a motion film: one per real press instead).
- Effects sit under the music; the voice is never masked.
- The music's tempo fits the cutting, and cuts land on its beats.
- No meme sound or UI click the picture doesn't call for.

skills.name: brand-application
skills.title: Brand application
skills.description: The kit applied with restraint: colours by role, fonts, logo files, tone.
skills.instructions:
Brand application: the kit, applied with restraint, so the video looks like the product and nothing else.

Rules
- Colours by role: the kit's background and text colours carry most of the frame; the accent appears once or twice per beat, on the thing that matters. Never a colour outside the kit (the style guide's palette counts).
- Fonts: the kit's families and weights only, its files loaded; one family for type unless the kit names a second for code or display.
- Logos: the kit's files only, the right one for the background (light, dark, mark), never redrawn, traced, recoloured, stretched or retyped. Clear space around it at least the height of its mark.
- Tone and copy: the kit's tone, its taglines and URLs exactly as written; plain words, no filler ("seamlessly", "unlock", "supercharge").
- Real product: the brief's real captures and screenshots, at their real colours.
- The project's theme uses the kit (update_project theme), so components and graphics match.

Do
- Use the kit's examples and style guide for grammar (shot lengths, transitions, type scale), never for content.
- Check the logo at phone size on the end card: it must be crisp and centred in its space.

Don't
- Don't invent a logo, an app icon, product UI, metrics, quotes or customer logos.
- Don't bring a reference video's colours or fonts into the kit.
- Don't decorate: no gradients, glows or textures the kit doesn't have.

Example
- Kit near-black background, off-white text, one green accent: titles off-white on near-black, the accent only on "4 minutes" and the CTA button, logo-light on the end card with its URL.

Review checklist
- Only the kit's colours, fonts and logo files are on screen.
- The logo is the kit's file, on a background it was made for, never distorted.
- The accent marks what matters, not everything.
- Copy matches the kit's tone; taglines and URLs are exact.
- Nothing invented: no fake UI, metrics, quotes or logos.

skills.name: make-brand-kit
skills.title: Make a brand kit
skills.description: Builds a brand kit from a link or dropped logos and pictures: asks a few questions, then saves the kit with the brand tools.
skills.instructions:
Builds a brand kit with the user, from a link to their site or the logos and pictures they drop in. Short questions first, then the kit, then show it.

Steps
- Ask first, on one ask_user card (freeText on): the brand's name; a link to its website, or the logo files and pictures they have (they can drop PNG or SVG files into the chat or paste a folder); and whether this kit is for every project or only this one. If the message already answers a question, don't ask it again.
- Then one more ask_user card when it isn't clear yet: the tone in a few words (for example calm and precise, or loud and playful), and anything to avoid (words, colours, styles).
- With a link: read the site (WebFetch, WebSearch for its press kit or brand page). Take the real logo files (SVG first, else a large PNG), the colours the site uses (hex, with their role: background, text, primary, accent, muted), the fonts it loads (and their font files when the site serves them), the tagline and real copy for taglines.
- With dropped files: the attached pictures are saved in the project's .cache/agent-images folder (the message lists their paths); a pasted path or folder is used as it is. Read each picture: a logo goes in logos (light for a dark background, dark for a light one, mark for a square symbol); take the colours from the logos and pictures.
- Write the kit with brand_write: name, colors with roles, fonts (with file when you have one), logos (paths or https addresses), tone, taglines, urls, dos and donts. scope project only when they said this project only.
- Then brand_read it and tell the user what went in and what's missing (a font without a file, no dark logo), in two or three lines. They can change anything in the Brand tab.

Rules
- Never invent a logo, colours, fonts or taglines: only what the site shows or the user gave. Ask when something is missing instead of guessing.
- Changing an existing kit's colours or fonts shows the user a before and after card; a new kit doesn't.
- A reference video or picture for a look goes in the kit's style (reference_frames, then brand_write style), never in its colours or fonts.

Review checklist
- The kit has the brand's real logo files, not a drawn or retyped logo.
- Every colour has a role and comes from the site or the user's files.
- Every font is the brand's own and has a file or is installed; else it says so.
- The tone, do's and don'ts are the user's words or the brand's own copy.

skills.name: loudness-rules
skills.title: Loudness rules
skills.description: Levels a mix by measurement: a target per platform, voice and music set from the exported numbers, true peak under the limiter.
skills.instructions:
Levels a finished edit from measured numbers. A gain picked by feel stays a guess until measure agrees.

Order
1. Clean first: echo-cleanup and audio.denoise change what gets measured.
2. Set the target once: {"op":"update_project","set":{"master":{"loudness":{"targetLufs":-14}}}}. update_project replaces master whole, so keep master.effects.
3. media_analyze loudness on each voice and music file: integrated LUFS, range, true peak, silences.
4. Level the voice with gainDb per clip, then the music against it, then effects.
5. measure {"what":"sound"} reports each role as exported and every effect against the voice, with the gain change it needs. Apply, then measure again.

Targets
- YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, X: -14 LUFS. Podcasts and long talks: -16. Broadcast: -23.
- True peak under -1 dBTP: the master limiter does this by default, so leave it on.

Balance
- The voice is the anchor.
- Music under speech: 15 to 20 dB below the voice, with audio.duck on its track (about -12 dB) doing the moving.
- Music alone, between lines: up to about 6 dB under where the voice sat.
- Effects: 6 to 12 dB under the music, never over a spoken word.
- Two speakers: within 2 dB of each other, clip by clip. A speaker's average can match while single clips sit 6 dB apart.
- A whole clip takes gainDb; a stretch inside one takes gainKeys (frames from the item's start, dB on top of gainDb).
- A gentle audio.compressor on the voice (ratio 2 to 4) evens phrases; try it before a long list of gainKeys.

What goes wrong
- The export moves the whole mix to the target, so master.gainDb is only heard with "As mixed". Trim sources.
- A boost lifts room noise with the voice. Past about +9 dB, add audio.denoise or tell the user the recording is the limit.
- Open mics add up: judge from measure, which reads the sum.
- Solo and mute left on change the export: project_read's mixNote says when.

Done means measure shows the master within 1 LU of the target and no effect flagged. Give the final numbers in your reply, as measured.

Review checklist
- The voice is never masked by music or effects.
- Music stays under speech and comes up only between lines.
- Effects sit under the music.
- Speakers sound level with each other from clip to clip.

skills.name: echo-cleanup
skills.title: Echo cleanup across mics
skills.description: Removes bleed and doubled voices from a recording with one mic per speaker, by lowering each open mic while another person talks.
skills.instructions:
For an interview, podcast or panel with one audio track per speaker. Each open mic also catches the others, later and quieter, and two mics together sound doubled. The cure is lowering whoever is silent at that moment. With one speaker or one mixed track there is nothing to separate: use audio.denoise. An echo recorded on every mic alike can't be fixed by gain: say so.

Find it
1. project_read: the speaker tracks, and that they line up in time.
2. transcript_read each mic, format words. The speaker's own mic is the louder one; bleed is often transcribed too, so one sentence on two mics is a clue.
3. media_analyze loudness on each mic: few silences (below -40 dB) while its speaker is quiet means strong bleed.
4. List who speaks when, merging gaps under 0.5 s. Most of an episode has one speaker, so only those windows need work.

Fix it
- Lower the silent mic with gainKeys on its clip (frames from the item's start): reach -8 dB over 3 to 5 frames just before the other person starts, return over 5 to 8 frames after they stop. Deeper only if needed; -20 dB makes the room pump.
- update_item replaces gainKeys whole, so read the clip first. A second pass replaces keys, never stacks them.
- audio.duck suits a long plain conversation: {"module":"audio.duck","params":{"under":["guest"],"amountDb":-10,"attackMs":40,"releaseMs":250,"thresholdDb":-28}} on the host's track, and the reverse on the guest's. Bleed can trip it, so raise thresholdDb until it opens only for that speaker. When you can't confirm that, use gainKeys.
- Keep what has no words: a laugh or a "mm" is content. Never delete a clip for an empty transcript; propose deletions with ask_user, each with its time.
- Real cross-talk stays: leave both mics up.

Check it
- You can't hear the result, and measure confirms levels only. Ask the user to listen to the two or three worst moments, with their times.
- Compare your keys with the word frames: no key may clip a first word.
- Then level with loudness-rules, keeping these keys. Report how many windows you lowered and by how much.

Review checklist
- No word loses its start or end to a lowered mic.
- Reactions and laughs are still in the edit.
- Real cross-talk keeps both voices.
- Nothing was deleted without the user's say.

skills.name: vertical-reframe
skills.title: Vertical reframing
skills.description: Turns 16:9 footage into a full-frame 9:16 cut: a framing per shot that follows the speaker, captions in the safe area, no clutter.
skills.instructions:
Turns wide talking footage into a 9:16 short that fills the frame. A 9:16 slice keeps under a third of a 16:9 picture's width, so a centre crop loses someone in any two-shot. Each shot gets its own framing, chosen by looking.

Setup
1. update_project set canvas to 1080 x 1920, same fps. Re-place text and graphics.
2. contact_sheet with at "shots" on the source; transcript_read for who talks when.
3. Plan a table: each shot's frames, who speaks, and that person's position as a share p of the picture's width, read off the frames.

Framing
- For 16:9 footage use a box taller than the crop needs: {"x":X,"y":0,"w":3413,"h":1920,"fit":"cover"}. To centre a person: X = 540 - 3413 × p, clamped to -2333..0. update_item replaces transform whole.
- split_item wherever the framing changes. Inside a shot, keys on x make a slow follow; across a camera change, jump.
- Follow whoever is talking. In a two-shot, cut sides on the turn of speech. Go to a listener only for a reaction worth seeing.
- Eyes about 40 % down the frame. Tighter means scale up to 1.2; recheck edges, since a lean can leave the frame.
- Both people at once: two clips, {"x":0,"y":0,"w":1080,"h":960,"fit":"cover"} and the same at y 960. Use it briefly.

Text
- captions_make with lines {"maxLines":2,"maxWords":4}, sentence case, one colour, one weight.
- Keep text out of the top 15 %, the bottom 35 % and the right 18 %.
- One hook line, gone by 3 s. A small logo in one corner is enough branding.

Keep it calm
- Hard cuts. No punch-in on every cut, no creeping zoom, no whip pans, no spring slam on text.
- No per-word colour flashes, emoji or uppercase captions unless asked.
- No blurred bars and no letterboxed wide picture.

Check
- render_frames with phone true at each cut and 1 s after it. A face at the edge, or the speaker off screen, fails the shot: fix its X.
- project_check for text position and size.

Review checklist
- The picture fills the 9:16 frame on every shot, no bars.
- Whoever is talking is on screen and inside the frame.
- Captions are in the safe area and readable at 360 px wide.
- Framing changes happen on cuts or as one slow move inside a shot.

skills.name: broll-over-dialogue
skills.title: B-roll over dialogue
skills.description: Lays real cutaways over a talking cut: picks moments from the transcript, keeps the dialogue audio, times each shot to the words.
skills.instructions:
Puts cutaways over talking footage while the voice carries on. The main track holds the dialogue; b-roll sits above it, muted, so the talk's timing never moves.

Prepare
1. Lock the talk first. Main-track cuts close up while other tracks stay put, so b-roll placed early falls out of sync.
2. Find shots: project_read for the project's media, media_search for the user's other projects, contact_sheet with at "shots" on each file. media_rank picks the cleanest and its best stretch.
3. transcript_read the main clip, with frames.

Pick moments
- Cover a line when the speaker names something you can show, when a jump cut needs hiding, or when one face has held too long.
- Open on the speaker so the audience meets them, and bring the face back for the main point.
- Match the meaning: "the workshop" gets the workshop. A shot merely near the topic reads as filler, so leave the moment and say what shot would help.
- Only footage the user gave you, or generated with their go-ahead.
- A quarter to a half of the runtime is a good ceiling unless the brief asks for more.

Place
- A video track above main (add_track kind "video"), then a muted clip per cutaway:
{"op":"insert_item","track":"broll","item":{"id":"broll-1","type":"clip","media":"m-shop","in":240,"start":312,"duration":75,"mute":true,"transform":{"fit":"cover"}}}
- Start a few frames before the named word. End on a sentence end or a pause.
- 2 to 4 s a shot; two or three in a row can cover a list. Under 1.5 s flickers unless it sits on a music beat.
- Keep in and duration inside the shot's good stretch.
- On 9:16, move x as in vertical-reframe so the subject stays in view.
- Hard cuts in and out. A cutaway's own sound, when it helps, goes in unmuted at about -20 dB under the voice: measure it.

Keep it working
- Captions and titles stay on tracks above the b-roll.
- After any later cut on main, re-read the frames and move each cutaway back onto its words.
- render_frames at each cutaway's first and last frame; contact_sheet of the edit for variety.

Review checklist
- Each cutaway shows what is being said at that moment.
- The speaker is on screen for the opening and the main point.
- No cutaway is under about 1.5 s or cuts in mid-word.
- Every shot is real footage from the project, filling the frame.

skills.name: cut-takes
skills.title: Cut takes
skills.description: Turns a long recording with retakes into a tight talk: reads the transcript, keeps the best take of each line, removes false starts.
skills.instructions:
Turns a raw recording with retakes, false starts and pauses into a clean spoken edit, working from the words. The picture is checked afterwards.

Read
1. transcript_read the whole take, every page (from = next.from). On a long take each text line is a phrase, and a retake sits on its own line.
2. media_analyze loudness gives silences; media_analyze video gives frozen or shaky stretches.
3. Several camera files of one script: media_rank says which is cleanest. Delivery is still chosen by the words.

Decide
- Group lines that say the same thing. Retakes repeat the opening words and often follow a stop or "sorry, again".
- Default to the last complete take of a line. Take an earlier one when the later one trails off or stumbles. render_frames both if eyes or framing might decide it.
- Remove false starts, abandoned sentences, repeated lines, talk to the crew, count-ins and anything around the real take.
- Keep asides that land, a real laugh, a pause that gives a point its weight.
- Cut whole phrases. One word out of the middle of a sentence leaves a jump in the voice.
- Two good versions with different content: ask_user once, with both lines and their times, then go on.

Cut
- List each kept line and each removed range with its reason first.
- transcript_edit with dryRun true: remove with word ranges ({"from":"w120","to":"w164"}, both ends included). Read the result, then run it for real as one edit.
- Second pass: pauses {"min":0.6} for a talk, 0.4 for a fast social cut, and fillers true. The "maybe" fillers (like, you know, so) are judged by hand and go in remove.
- Leave a breath between sentences; no air at all sounds machine-made.

Check
- transcript_read again: the kept text reads as clean prose, no line twice.
- A picture jump at a cut is normal for talking footage. Cover it with broll-over-dialogue, or a small scale change on the next clip (scale 1.08).
- render_frames at a few cuts: no held blink, no mouth stuck open.
- Other tracks don't move with main: re-check music, titles and b-roll.
- Report the length before and after, and any line you left as a question.

Review checklist
- No line is said twice in the edit.
- No sentence is left unfinished.
- Spoken cuts fall between phrases.
- Titles, music and captions still line up with the words.

skills.name: motion-film
skills.title: Motion film
skills.description: Facts for a motion film on the real UI or footage: honesty about the run, the defects Uncut measures and blocks, the toolkit. The creative direction is yours, or a Template's.
skills.instructions:
Facts for a motion film, no creative direction: the story, look, pacing and sound come from the user's message, or from a Template (#111, Templates in the / menu) when one is picked.

The user's direction comes first
- Follow the message as written: its structure, look, timings, sizes, sound and bans. What it leaves open, decide for this film; nothing here is a house style.
- Run facts stay true and measured defects stay defects, whatever the brief says.

Honesty
- On-screen facts about this run are real results only: a review reads "Reviewing" until one passes; no invented counts, scores, timings or statuses.
- Product UI, numbers and quotes come from the brief, the kit or real captures. The kit's logos and Claude mark go in as their files (brand_read), never redrawn. A missing asset is asked for, not mocked up.

Defects Uncut measures (the critic's scan; they block a review)
- Hard cuts: a one-frame jump, or most of the picture swapped in 2 to 3 frames (a quick swap); carry one state into the next instead.
- Single-frame pops and 2 to 3 frame flashes: something drawn whole for a frame or two, then gone.
- Near-empty or low-information frames: bare canvas, a cursor or a speck, for 0.33 s; tiny text in a big flat field for 0.5 s.
- Text cut at the frame's edge.
- Key text illegible at phone size (360 px wide), a desktop-sized panel the moment is about included.
These are facts about the render, not taste: render_frames around each move before review_submit.

Toolkit (docs_read graphics)
- uncutUI (uncut:lib/ui.js): Uncut's real UI as parts, the live editor stage (uncutUI.mount "editor"), uncutUI.sequence for large pieces morphing into each other, uncutUI.fly for an element travelling between them.
- uncutMotion (uncut:lib/motion.js): uncutMotion.click for a cursor press, uncutMotion.camera for moves and push-ins, uncutMotion.grow for a shot growing out of a shape, uncutMotion.frameRect with safe and keep to frame a UI rect without cutting its text.
- render(t) a pure function of t; beat_grid for the music's real beats when the film moves to music.

Review checklist
- The user's message is followed: its structure, look, timings and bans.
- Numbers and statuses about this run are true, else none; a review reads "Reviewing" until it passes.
- No hard cut or quick swap the message doesn't ask for.
- No single-frame pop or 2 to 3 frame flash.
- No near-empty or low-information frame (0.33 s bare, 0.5 s tiny text).
- No text cut at the frame's edge; key text reads at 360 px wide.
- Logos and the Claude mark are the kit's files; nothing invented or redrawn.
